runs.input: A detector runs m=3 switches. A hidden mask X of copy boundaries is drawn. With forced mask F, cuts occur at X union F; each segment of length j contributes a_j to the chance all three switches pass, and segment probabilities multiply. Infer P(X=empty), P(X={1}), P(X={2}), P(X={1,2}) as fractions in this order. Can a possible additional copy after switch 3 change those four rates? Give the fractions and final answer concisely.
runs.reply: To infer the probabilities of the hidden mask X, we need to consider the probabilities of the four observed survival probabilities for the switch 3. The probabilities of the four observed survival probabilities are given as 7/32, 5/32, 5/32, and 1/8. Since the hidden mask X is a union of three switches, we can use the principle of inclusion-exclusion to find the probability of the union of the four observed probabilities.
